questions.prompt: A particle moves along the \(x\)-axis with acceleration \[a(t)=2t-10+\frac{12}{t},\qquad t>1.\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find an expression for the velocity \(v(t)\), given that \(v(1)=9\).
parts.answer: Integrating acceleration gives \[v(t)=t^2-10t+12\ln t+C.\]Using \(v(1)=9\) gives \(C=18\). Thus \[\boxed{v(t)=t^2-10t+12\ln t+18}.\]

parts.prompt: For \(1\le t\le3\), at what value of \(t\) is the velocity a maximum? Justify.

questions.prompt: A rectangle has constant area \(200\) square meters. Its length \(L\) is increasing at \(4\) meters per second.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the width \(W\) at the instant when the width is decreasing at \(0.5\) meter per second.
parts.answer: From \(LW=200\), \[L\frac{dW}{dt}+W\frac{dL}{dt}=0.\]At the stated instant, \(dW/dt=-\frac12\) and \(dL/dt=4\), so \(-\frac12L+4W=0\), or \(L=8W\). Combining this with \(LW=200\) gives \(8W^2=200\), so \[\boxed{W=5\text{ m}}.\]

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: At what rate is the diagonal \(D\) changing when \(W=10\) meters?
parts.answer: When \(W=10\), constant area gives \(L=20\). Also \[\frac{dW}{dt}=-\frac{W}{L}\frac{dL}{dt}=-2.\]Since \(D^2=L^2+W^2\), \[2D\frac{dD}{dt}=2L\frac{dL}{dt}+2W\frac{dW}{dt}.\]Here \(D=\sqrt{20^2+10^2}=10\sqrt5\), so \[\frac{dD}{dt}=\frac{20(4)+10(-2)}{10\sqrt5}=\boxed{\frac6{\sqrt5}=\frac{6\sqrt5}{5}\text{ m/s}}.\]

questions.prompt: Let \[f(x)=\sin^3 x+\sin^3|x|.\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find \(f'(x)\) for \(x>0\).
parts.answer: For \(x>0\), \(|x|=x\), so \(f(x)=2\sin^3x\). Therefore \[\boxed{f'(x)=6\sin^2x\cos x}.\]

questions.prompt: Given the function \(f(x)=x^3-x^2-4x+4\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the zeros of \(f\).
parts.answer: Factor by grouping: \[f(x)=x^2(x-1)-4(x-1)=(x-1)(x-2)(x+2).\] Hence the zeros are \[\boxed{x=-2,\ 1,\ 2}.\]

parts.answer: The tangent at \(x=a\) gives \(-8=f(a)-af^{\prime}(a)\). Since \[f(a)-af^{\prime}(a)=-2a^3+a^2+4,\]we obtain \[2a^3-a^2-12=0=(a-2)(2a^2+3a+6).\]The quadratic has no real roots, so \(a=2\), and \(b=f(2)=0\). Thus \[\boxed{(a,b)=(2,0)}.\]

questions.prompt: Let \(f(x)=(1-x)^2\) for all real \(x\), let \(g(x)=\ln x\) for \(x>0\), and let \(h(x)=(1-\ln x)^2\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Determine whether \(h=f\circ g\) or \(h=g\circ f\).
parts.answer: \[f(g(x))=(1-\ln x)^2=h(x).\] Therefore \[\boxed{h=f\circ g}.\]

parts.prompt: Sketch the graph of \(h\), showing important features.
parts.answer: The domain is \(x>0\). The graph decreases on \((0,e)\), has absolute minimum \((e,0)\), and increases on \((e,\infty)\). questions.prompt: Given \[f(x)=\frac{2x-2}{x^2+x-2}.\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: For what values of \(x\) is \(f\) discontinuous?
parts.answer: \[x^2+x-2=(x-1)(x+2),\]so the denominator is zero at \(x=1\) and \(x=-2\). Thus \[\boxed{x=-2,\ 1}.\]

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: At each discontinuity, determine whether \(\lim_{x\to a}f(x)\) exists and give its value when it exists.
parts.answer: For \(x\ne1,-2\), \[f(x)=\frac{2(x-1)}{(x-1)(x+2)}=\frac2{x+2}.\] Therefore \[\boxed{\lim_{x\to1}f(x)=\frac23}.\]At \(x=-2\), the one-sided limits are opposite infinities, so the two-sided limit does not exist.

questions.prompt: A particle moves on the \(x\)-axis with velocity \(v(t)=\sin(2t)\). At \(t=0\), the particle is at the origin.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: For \(0\le t\le\pi\), find all values of \(t\) for which the particle is moving to the left.
parts.answer: The particle moves left when \(v(t)<0\). On \(0<t<\pi\), \(\sin(2t)<0\) exactly when \[\boxed{\frac\pi2<t<\pi}.\]

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Write an expression for the position \(s(t)\).
parts.answer: \[s(t)=s(0)+\int_0^t\sin(2u)\,du=\left[-\frac12\cos(2u)\right]_0^t.\]Thus \[\boxed{s(t)=\frac{1-\cos(2t)}2}.\]

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: For \(0\le t\le\dfrac\pi2\), find the average value of the position function determined in part (b).
parts.answer: The average value on \([0,\pi/2]\) is \[\frac{2}{\pi}\int_0^{\pi/2}\frac{1-\cos(2t)}2\,dt=\frac{1}{\pi}\left[t-\frac12\sin(2t)\right]_0^{\pi/2}=\boxed{\frac12}.\]

questions.prompt: Given the curve \[x^2-xy+y^2=9.\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Write a general expression for the slope \(dy/dx\).
parts.answer: Differentiating implicitly gives \[2x-(xy^{\prime}+y)+2yy^{\prime}=0.\]Therefore \[(2y-x)y^{\prime}=y-2x,\qquad\boxed{y^{\prime}=\frac{y-2x}{2y-x}}.\]

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the coordinates of the points where the tangents are vertical.
parts.answer: Vertical tangents occur when \(2y-x=0\), provided the numerator is nonzero. Set \(x=2y\): \[4y^2-2y^2+y^2=9\Rightarrow 3y^2=9.\]Thus \[\boxed{(2\sqrt3,\sqrt3)\quad\text{and}\quad(-2\sqrt3,-\sqrt3)}.\]

parts.prompt: At \((0,3)\), find the rate of change of the slope with respect to \(x\).
parts.answer: First, \(y^{\prime}(0,3)=1/2\). Differentiating \(2x-xy^{\prime}-y+2yy^{\prime}=0\) again gives \[(2y-x)y^{\prime\prime}+2-2y^{\prime}+2(y^{\prime})^2=0.\]At \((0,3)\), \[6y^{\prime\prime}+2-1+\frac12=0,\]so \[\boxed{y^{\prime\prime}=-\frac14}.\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the maximum area of a rectangle with two vertices on the \(x\)-axis and two vertices on the graph of \(f\). Justify.
parts.answer: Let the upper-right vertex be \((x,e^{-x^2})\), \(x>0\). Symmetry gives \[A(x)=2xe^{-x^2}.\]Then \[A^{\prime}(x)=2e^{-x^2}(1-2x^2),\]so the only positive critical point is \(x=1/\sqrt2\). The derivative changes from positive to negative there, so \[\boxed{A_{\max}=\sqrt{\frac2e}}.\]

questions.prompt: Let \(g\) and \(h\) be twice-differentiable for all real \(x\), and suppose that for every \(x\): \[(g(x))^2+(h(x))^2=1,\qquad g^{\prime}(x)=(h(x))^2,\qquad h(x)>0,\qquad g(0)=0.\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Justify that \(h^{\prime}(x)=-g(x)h(x)\) for every \(x\).
parts.answer: Differentiate \(g^2+h^2=1\): \[2gg^{\prime}+2hh^{\prime}=0.\]Since \(g^{\prime}=h^2\) and \(h>0\), \[h^{\prime}=-\frac{gg^{\prime}}h=-\frac{gh^2}h=\boxed{-gh}.\]

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Justify that \(h\) has a relative maximum at \(x=0\).
parts.answer: From the identity and \(g(0)=0\), positivity gives \(h(0)=1\). Also \(h^{\prime}(0)=0\). Differentiating \(h^{\prime}=-gh\) gives \[h^{\prime\prime}=-g^{\prime}h-gh^{\prime}.\]Thus \(h^{\prime\prime}(0)=-(1)(1)-0=-1<0\), so \[\boxed{h\text{ has a relative maximum at }x=0}.\]

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Justify that the graph of \(g\) has a point of inflection at \(x=0\).
parts.answer: Because \(g^{\prime}=h^2>0\), \(g\) is strictly increasing. Since \(g(0)=0\), we have \(g(x)<0\) for \(x<0\) and \(g(x)>0\) for \(x>0\). Also \[g^{\prime\prime}=2hh^{\prime}=-2gh^2.\]Therefore \(g^{\prime\prime}>0\) to the left of 0 and \(g^{\prime\prime}<0\) to the right. Concavity changes at \(0\), so \[\boxed{(0,0)\text{ is an inflection point of }g}.\]

questions.prompt: Find the maximum volume of an open-top box made by cutting equal squares from the corners of an \(8\)-inch by \(15\)-inch sheet and folding up the sides. Justify your answer.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the maximum volume and justify.
parts.answer:
If each cut has side length \(x\), then
\[V(x)=x(8-2x)(15-2x),\qquad 0\le x\le4.\]
Differentiation gives
\[V^{\prime}(x)=12x^2-92x+120=4(3x-5)(x-6).\]
The only feasible interior critical point is \(x=5/3\). The derivative changes from positive to negative there, and the endpoint volumes are zero. Therefore
\[\boxed{V_{\max}=V\left(\frac53\right)=\frac{2450}{27}\approx90.741\text{ in}^3}.\]

questions.prompt: Let \(R\) be the region bounded by \(y=\dfrac{\ln x}{x}\), the \(x\)-axis, and the line \(x=e\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the area of \(R\).
parts.answer:
The curve meets the \(x\)-axis at \(x=1\). Therefore
\[A=\int_1^e\frac{\ln x}{x}\,dx
=\left[\frac12(\ln x)^2\right]_1^e
=\boxed{\frac12}.\]

\[V=2\pi[(x\ln x-x)]_1^e=\boxed{2\pi}.\]

questions.prompt: Let \(f(x)=x^3+ax^2+bx+c\). The graph has an inflection point at \((0,-2)\), and the average value of \(f\) on \([0,2]\) is \(-3\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Determine \(a\), \(b\), and \(c\).
parts.answer:
The point condition gives \(c=-2\). Since
\[f^{\prime\prime}(x)=6x+2a\]
and the inflection occurs at \(x=0\), \(a=0\). Hence \(f(x)=x^3+bx-2\). The average value condition gives
\[-3=\frac12\int_0^2(x^3+bx-2)\,dx=\frac12(4+2b-4)=b.\]
Thus
\[\boxed{a=0,\quad b=-3,\quad c=-2}.\]

The secant slope is
\[\frac{f(3)-f(0)}{3}=\frac{16-(-2)}3=6.\]
Set \(f^{\prime}(x)=3x^2-3=6\):

Only the value in \((0,3)\) is

questions.prompt: Let \(R\) be the region in the first quadrant bounded by \(y=x^3\) and \(y=\sqrt{x}\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the area of \(R\).
parts.answer:
The curves meet at \(x=0\) and \(x=1\). On this interval, \(\sqrt{x}\ge x^3\). Therefore
\[A=\int_0^1(\sqrt{x}-x^3)dx
=\left[\frac23x^{3/2}-\frac14x^4\right]_0^1
=\boxed{\frac5{12}}.\]

parts.prompt: Find the volume generated when \(R\) is revolved about the \(x\)-axis.
parts.answer:
Using washers,
\[V=\pi\int_0^1\left[(\sqrt{x})^2-(x^3)^2\right]dx
=\pi\int_0^1(x-x^6)dx.\]
Thus
\[V=\pi\left[\frac{x^2}{2}-\frac{x^7}{7}\right]_0^1
=\boxed{\frac{5\pi}{14}}.\]

questions.prompt: A rectangle with sides parallel to the coordinate axes is inscribed under the parabola \(y=-4x^2+4\), symmetric about the \(y\)-axis. Its upper-right vertex is \(C=(x,y)\), where \(0<x<1\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the coordinates of \(C\) when the rectangle has maximum area.
parts.answer:
The rectangle has width \(2x\) and height \(4-4x^2\), so
\[A(x)=2x(4-4x^2)=8x-8x^3.\]
Then \(A^{\prime}(x)=8-24x^2\), giving \(x=1/\sqrt3\). This is a maximum because \(A^{\prime}\) changes from positive to negative. Hence
\[\boxed{C=\left(\frac1{\sqrt3},\frac83\right)}.\]

questions.prompt: Let \(f(x)=\ln(x^2)\) for \(x>0\), and let \(g(x)=e^{2x}\) for \(x>0\). Define \(H=f\circ g\) and \(K=g\circ f\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the domain and a simplified formula for \(H\).
parts.answer:
Because \(g\) is defined for \(x>0\) and always has positive output,
\[
H(x)=\ln\bigl((e^{2x})^2\bigr)=\ln(e^{4x})=4x.
\]
Thus
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{Dom}(H)=(0,\infty),\qquad H(x)=4x}.
\]

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the domain and a simplified formula for \(K\).
parts.answer:
For \(K(x)=g(f(x))\), the input to \(g\) must be strictly positive:
\[
\ln(x^2)>0\Longleftrightarrow x^2>1.
\]
Together with the original restriction \(x>0\), this gives \(x>1\). Also
\[
K(x)=e^{2\ln(x^2)}=x^4.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{\operatorname{Dom}(K)=(1,\infty),\qquad K(x)=x^4}.
\]

questions.prompt: A particle moves along a line with acceleration \(a(t)=10e^{2t}\), initial velocity \(v(0)=5\), and initial position \(s(0)=0\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the velocity function.
parts.answer:
Integrating,
\[v(t)=5e^{2t}+C.\]
Since \(v(0)=5\), \(C=0\). Hence
\[\boxed{v(t)=5e^{2t}}.\]

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the distance traveled while the velocity increases from \(5\) to \(15\).
parts.answer:
Velocity reaches 15 when \(5e^{2t}=15\), so \(t=\frac12\ln3\). Since velocity is positive, distance equals displacement:
\[\int_0^{(1/2)\ln3}5e^{2t}dt
=\frac52[e^{2t}]_0^{(1/2)\ln3}
=\frac52(3-1)=\boxed{5}.\]

Integrating velocity,

Using \(s(0)=0\) gives \(C=-5/2\). Therefore

questions.prompt:
A continuous function \(f\) satisfies
\[x^4-5x^2(f(x))^2+4(f(x))^4=0\]
for every real \(x\), and its graph contains \((2,1)\) and \((-2,-2)\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find a general expression for \(dy/dx\) on the implicit curve.
parts.answer:
Differentiating
\[x^4-5x^2y^2+4y^4=0\]
gives
\[4x^3-10xy^2-10x^2yy^{\prime}+16y^3y^{\prime}=0.\]
Therefore
\[\boxed{y^{\prime}=\frac{2x^3-5xy^2}{5x^2y-8y^3}}.\]

questions.prompt:
Define
\[f(x)=\begin{cases}
1+2p(x-1)+(x-1)^2,&x\le1,\\
qx+p,&x>1.
\end{cases}\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the relation between \(p\) and \(q\) required for continuity at \(x=1\).
parts.answer:
The left value is \(f(1)=1\). The right-hand limit is \(q+p\). Continuity requires
\[\boxed{p+q=1},\qquad\text{equivalently }\boxed{q=1-p}.\]

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the values of \(p\) and \(q\) for which \(f'\) is continuous at \(x=1\).
parts.answer:
For \(f'\) to exist and be continuous at the join, \(f\) must first be continuous, so \(p+q=1\). The one-sided derivative values are \(2p\) and \(q\), so continuity of \(f'\) requires \(q=2p\). Solving
\[
p+q=1,\qquad q=2p
\]
gives
\[
\boxed{p=\frac13,\qquad q=\frac23}.
\]

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: If \(p\) and \(q\) have the values determined in part (b), is \(f''\) a continuous function? Justify your answer.
parts.answer:
For \(x<1\), \(f^{\prime\prime}(x)=2\). For \(x>1\), \(f^{\prime\prime}(x)=0\). The first derivative is continuous at 1, but its one-sided slopes do not agree, so \(f^{\prime\prime}(1)\) does not exist. Hence
\[\boxed{f^{\prime\prime}\text{ is not continuous on }\mathbb R}.\]
Historical scoring sometimes treated “continuous on its domain” separately; the modern precise statement is that \(f^{\prime\prime}\) is undefined at the join.

questions.prompt:
Let \(f\) be the function defined by
\[
f(x)=x^4-3x^2+2.
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the zeros of \(f\).
parts.answer:
Factor:
\[
f(x)=(x^2-1)(x^2-2).
\]
Thus the zeros are
\[
\boxed{x=-\sqrt2,-1,1,\sqrt2}.
\]

Since \(f(1)=0\) and

f'(x)=4x^3-6x,
\]
we have \(f'(1)=-2\). Therefore
\[
\boxed{y=-2x+2}.
\]

parts.answer:
Parallel tangents have slope \(-2\), so
\[
4x^3-6x=-2.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
2x^3-3x+1=(x-1)(2x^2+2x-1)=0.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{x=1,\quad x=\frac{-1+\sqrt3}{2},\quad x=\frac{-1-\sqrt3}{2}}.
\]

questions.prompt:
Let \(R\) be the first-quadrant region enclosed by
\[
y=4-x^2,\qquad y=3x,
\]
and the \(y\)-axis.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the area of \(R\).
parts.answer:
The curves meet where \(4-x^2=3x\), giving \(x=1\) in the first quadrant. Thus
\[
A=\int_0^1\bigl((4-x^2)-3x\bigr)\,dx
=\left[4x-\frac{x^3}{3}-\frac{3x^2}{2}\right]_0^1
=\boxed{\frac{13}{6}}.
\]

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the volume formed by revolving \(R\) about the \(x\)-axis.
parts.answer:
Using washers,
\[
V=\pi\int_0^1\left[(4-x^2)^2-(3x)^2\right]dx.
\]
Therefore
\[
V=\pi\int_0^1(16-17x^2+x^4)\,dx
=\boxed{\frac{158\pi}{15}}.
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the intervals on which \(f\) is increasing.
parts.answer:
For \(x\ne0\),
\[
f'(x)=8x^{-1/3}-4.
\]
The derivative is positive only for \(0<x<8\). Thus \(f\) is increasing on
\[
\boxed{(0,8)}.
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Determine whether \(f\) is even or odd, and justify.
parts.answer:
Because the exponent depends on \(x^2\),
\[
f(-x)=5^{\sqrt{2(-x)^2-1}}=f(x).
\]
Therefore \(\boxed{f\text{ is even}}\).

questions.prompt:
Define
\[
f(x)=\begin{cases}
2x+1,&x\le2,\\
\frac12x^2+k,&x>2.
\end{cases}
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: For what value of \(k\) is \(f\) continuous at \(x=2\)?
parts.answer:
Continuity requires
\[
5=f(2)=\lim_{x\to2^+}\left(\frac12x^2+k\right)=2+k.
\]
Hence \(\boxed{k=3}\).

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Using that value of \(k\), determine whether \(f\) is differentiable at \(x=2\), using the definition.
parts.answer:
For \(k=3\), the function is continuous. The left difference quotient tends to \(2\). On the right,
\[
\frac{\frac12(2+h)^2+3-5}{h}=\frac{2h+\frac12h^2}{h}=2+\frac h2\to2.
\]
Both one-sided derivatives equal \(2\), so \(\boxed{f\text{ is differentiable at }2}\).

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Let \(k=4\). Determine whether \(f\) is differentiable at \(x=4\).
parts.answer: A neighbourhood of \(x=4\) lies entirely in the polynomial branch \(\frac12x^2+4\). Therefore \(f'(4)=4\), and \(\boxed{f\text{ is differentiable at }4}\).

questions.prompt:
A particle moves along the \(x\)-axis with position
\[
x(t)=\sin(\pi t^2),\qquad -1\le t\le1.
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the velocity.
parts.answer:
\[
v(t)=x'(t)=\boxed{2\pi t\cos(\pi t^2)}.
\]

\]

parts.prompt: For what values of \(t\) does the particle change direction?
parts.answer:
The velocity vanishes at
\[
t=0,\qquad t=\pm\frac1{\sqrt2}.

\[
\boxed{t=-\frac1{\sqrt2},\ 0,\ \frac1{\sqrt2}}.
\]

questions.prompt:
Let \(f\) be continuous on the real numbers and suppose
\[
\int_1^3 f(x)\,dx=\frac52,
\qquad
\int_1^5 f(x)\,dx=10.
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the average value of \(f\) on \([1,3]\).
parts.answer:
\[
f_{\mathrm{avg}}=\frac1{3-1}\int_1^3f(x)\,dx=\boxed{\frac54}.
\]

parts.label: (b)
parts.answer:
First,
\[
\int_3^5f(x)\,dx=10-\frac52=\frac{15}{2}.
\]
Hence
\[
\int_3^5(2f(x)+6)\,dx=2\left(\frac{15}{2}\right)+6(2)=\boxed{27}.
\]

parts.prompt: Given \(f(x)=ax+b\), find \(a\) and \(b\).
parts.answer:
The two integral conditions give
\[
4a+2b=\frac52,
\qquad
12a+4b=10.
\]
Solving yields
\[
\boxed{a=\frac54,\qquad b=-\frac54}.
\]

questions.prompt:
A particle moves on the \(x\)-axis with
\[
a(t)=\frac3{t^2},\qquad t>0.
\]
At \(t=1\), its position is \(6\) and its velocity is \(2\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find \(v(t)\).
parts.answer:
Integrating acceleration,
\[
v(t)=-\frac3t+C.
\]
Since \(v(1)=2\), \(C=5\). Thus
\[
\boxed{v(t)=5-\frac3t}.
\]

questions.prompt:
Let
\[
f(x)=\frac{x^3-x}{x^3-4x},
\]
with its original algebraic domain.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find \(\lim_{x\to0}f(x)\).
parts.answer:
For \(x\ne0\),
\[
f(x)=\frac{x^2-1}{x^2-4}.
\]
Therefore
\[
\boxed{\lim_{x\to0}f(x)=\frac14}.
\]

parts.answer:
The numerator vanishes at \(x=0,\pm1\), but \(x=0\) is excluded from the original domain. Hence the zeros are

\boxed{x=-1,1}.
\]

questions.prompt:
Let \(R\) be the first-quadrant region bounded by
\[
y=\tan x,
\]
the \(x\)-axis, and \(x=\pi/3\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the area of \(R\).
parts.answer:
\[
A=\int_0^{\pi/3}\tan x\,dx
=\left[-\ln(\cos x)\right]_0^{\pi/3}
=\boxed{\ln2}.
\]

questions.prompt:
A \(15\)-foot ladder leans against a wall. Its lower end moves away from the wall at
\[
\frac{dx}{dt}=\frac12\ \text{ft/s}.
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find \(dy/dt\) when the lower end is \(9\) feet from the wall.
parts.answer:
From \(x^2+y^2=225\), when \(x=9\), \(y=12\). Differentiating,
\[
2x\frac{dx}{dt}+2y\frac{dy}{dt}=0.
\]
Thus
\[
\boxed{\frac{dy}{dt}=-\frac38\ \text{ft/s}}.
\]

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find the rate of change of the triangle area at that instant.
parts.answer:
The area is \(A=\frac12xy\). Therefore
\[
\frac{dA}{dt}=\frac12\left(x\frac{dy}{dt}+y\frac{dx}{dt}\right)
=\frac12\left(9\left(-\frac38\right)+12\left(\frac12\right)\right)
=\boxed{\frac{21}{16}\ \text{ft}^2/\text{s}}.
\]

questions.prompt:
Let
\[
f(x)=(x^2+1)e^{-x},\qquad -4\le x\le4.
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find where \(f\) reaches its absolute maximum.
parts.answer:
\[
f'(x)=e^{-x}(2x-x^2-1)=-e^{-x}(x-1)^2\le0.
\]
Thus \(f\) is nonincreasing on the entire interval, so its absolute maximum occurs at
\[
\boxed{x=-4}.
\]

questions.prompt: An open-top rectangular tank has width \(4\) metres and volume \(36\) cubic metres. The base costs $10 per square metre and the sides cost $5 per square metre.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the cost of the least expensive tank.
parts.answer:
Let the length be \(l\) and height be \(h\). The volume condition is
\[
4lh=36,\qquad lh=9.
\]
The cost is
\[
C=40l+5(2lh+8h)=40l+90+40h.
\]
Using \(l=9/h\),
\[
C(h)=\frac{360}{h}+90+40h.
\]
Then \(C'(h)=-360/h^2+40=0\) gives \(h=3\), hence \(l=3\). The minimum cost is
\[
\boxed{\$330}.
\]

questions.prompt:
For every real \(x\), \(f\) is differentiable and even:
\[
f(-x)=f(x).
\]
Suppose \(f(p)=1\) and \(f'(p)=5\) for some \(p>0\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find \(f'(-p)\).
parts.answer:
Differentiating \(f(-x)=f(x)\) gives
\[
-f'(-x)=f'(x).
\]
Thus \(f'\) is odd and
\[
\boxed{f'(-p)=-5}.
\]

questions.prompt:
Let
\[
f(x)=x+\sin^2x,
\qquad
\frac\pi6\le x\le\frac{5\pi}{6}.
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find all \(x\) for which \(f'(x)=1\).
parts.answer:
\[
f'(x)=1+\sin(2x).
\]
Thus \(f'(x)=1\) when \(\sin(2x)=0\). In the interval, this gives
\[
\boxed{x=\frac\pi2}.
\]

questions.prompt: At \(t=0\), a jogger moves at \(300\) metres per minute. The acceleration is negative and directly proportional to \(t\), and the jogger stops at \(t=10\) minutes.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the velocity function.
parts.answer:
Write \(a(t)=-kt\). Then
\[
v(t)=300-\frac{k}{2}t^2.
\]
Since \(v(10)=0\), \(k=6\). Therefore
\[
\boxed{v(t)=300-3t^2}.
\]

parts.prompt: Find the total distance travelled in the ten-minute interval.
parts.answer:
The velocity is nonnegative on \([0,10]\), so
\[
D=\int_0^{10}(300-3t^2)\,dt
=\left[300t-t^3\right]_0^{10}
=\boxed{2000\ \text{metres}}.
\]

questions.prompt:
Let \(R\) be the first-quadrant region bounded by
\[
y=8-x^{3/2},
\]
the coordinate axes.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the area of \(R\).
parts.answer:
The curve meets the \(x\)-axis at \(x=4\). Thus
\[
A=\int_0^4(8-x^{3/2})\,dx
=\boxed{\frac{96}{5}}.
\]

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find \(k\) so that \(x=k\) divides the revolved solid into equal volumes.
parts.answer:
The required value satisfies
\[
\pi\int_0^k(8-x^{3/2})^2\,dx=\frac12\cdot\frac{576\pi}{5}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
64k-\frac{32}{5}k^{5/2}+\frac{k^4}{4}=\frac{288}{5}.
\]
The unique solution in \((0,4)\) is
\[
\boxed{k\approx0.995}.
\]

questions.prompt:
Let
\[
f(x)=\frac{x+\sin x}{\cos x},
\qquad -\frac\pi2<x<\frac\pi2.
\]

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: State whether \(f\) is even or odd and justify.
parts.answer:
The numerator is odd and the denominator is even, so
\[
f(-x)=-f(x).
\]
Thus \(\boxed{f\text{ is odd}}\).

questions.prompt: A continuous function \(f\) on \([-3,3]\) satisfies \(f(-3)=4\) and \(f(3)=1\). Its derivative and second derivative have the signs shown in the source table.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find all absolute maximum and minimum \(x\)-coordinates.
parts.answer:
The function increases on \((-3,-1)\) and decreases on \((-1,3)\), so the absolute maximum occurs at
\[
\boxed{x=-1}.
\]
The minimum must occur at an endpoint; since \(f(3)=1<f(-3)=4\), the absolute minimum occurs at
\[
\boxed{x=3}.
\]

questions.prompt:
For a cone,
\[
V=\frac13\pi r^2h.
\]
Suppose \(dV/dt=28\pi\), and at the instant in question \(r=3\), \(V=12\pi\), and \(dr/dt=1/2\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the rate of change of the base area.
parts.answer:
The base area is \(A=\pi r^2\), so
\[
\frac{dA}{dt}=2\pi r\frac{dr}{dt}=2\pi(3)\left(\frac12\right)=\boxed{3\pi}.
\]

rubric.rubricType: ECHS analytic practice rubric based on independent mathematical verification; not an official College Board point-by-point scoring guideline.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find \(dh/dt\).
parts.answer:
First, \(12\pi=\frac13\pi(3)^2h\), so \(h=4\). Differentiating the volume equation,
\[
28\pi=\frac13\pi\left(2rh\frac{dr}{dt}+r^2\frac{dh}{dt}\right).
\]
Substitution gives
\[
28=4+3\frac{dh}{dt},
\]
so
\[
\boxed{\frac{dh}{dt}=8}.
\]

parts.label: (c)

parts.answer:
\[
\frac{dA}{dh}=\frac{dA/dt}{dh/dt}=\frac{3\pi}{8}.
\]
Thus
\[
\boxed{\frac{dA}{dh}=\frac{3\pi}{8}}.
\]

questions.prompt:
Let \(R\) be enclosed by
\[
y=e^{-x},\qquad y=e^x,
\]
and \(x=\ln4\).

The curves meet at \(x=0\). Therefore
\[
A=\int_0^{\ln4}(e^x-e^{-x})\,dx
=\left[e^x+e^{-x}\right]_0^{\ln4}
=\boxed{\frac94}.
\]

questions.prompt:
Let
\[
f(x)=14\pi x^2,
\qquad
g(x)=k^2\sin\left(\frac{\pi x}{2k}\right),
\qquad k>0.
\]

parts.answer:
\[
f_{\mathrm{avg}}=\frac13\int_1^4 14\pi x^2\,dx
=\boxed{98\pi}.
\]

parts.answer:

\boxed{k=7\pi}.
\]

questions.prompt:
A balloon consists of a cylinder of radius \(r\) and height \(h\), capped by two hemispheres of radius \(r\). Thus
\[
V=\pi r^2h+\frac43\pi r^3.
\]
Suppose \(dV/dt=261\pi\). At the instant considered, \(r=3\), \(V=144\pi\), and \(dr/dt=2\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find the cylinder height.
parts.answer:
\[
144\pi=9\pi h+36\pi,
\]
so
\[
\boxed{h=12\ \text{cm}}.
\]

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Find how fast the cylinder height is increasing.
parts.answer:
Differentiate:
\[
\frac{dV}{dt}=2\pi rh\frac{dr}{dt}+\pi r^2\frac{dh}{dt}+4\pi r^2\frac{dr}{dt}.
\]
Substitution gives
\[
261\pi=144\pi+9\pi\frac{dh}{dt}+72\pi.
\]
Hence
\[
\boxed{\frac{dh}{dt}=5\ \text{cm/min}}.
\]

questions.prompt: The source graph shows \(f'\) on \([-3,3]\). It crosses the \(x\)-axis at \(x=-2\) and \(x=0\), and touches it at \(x=2\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Find all relative maxima and minima of \(f\).
parts.answer:
At \(x=-2\), \(f'\) changes from positive to negative, so \(f\) has a relative maximum there. At \(x=0\), \(f'\) changes from negative to positive, so \(f\) has a relative minimum there. At \(x=2\), the derivative does not change sign. Thus
\[
\boxed{\text{relative maximum at }x=-2;\quad\text{relative minimum at }x=0}.
\]

questions.prompt:
Define
\[
f(x)=\begin{cases}|x-1|+2,&x<1,\\ax^2+bx,&x\ge1,\end{cases}
\]
where \(a\) and \(b\) are constants.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: If \(a=2\) and \(b=3\), is \(f\) continuous for all \(x\)? Justify.
parts.answer: No. The left limit at \(1\) is \(2\), while \(f(1)=a+b=5\).

parts.answer: Continuity at the join requires \(\boxed{a+b=2}\).

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Find \(a,b\) for which \(f\) is both continuous and differentiable.
parts.answer:
For \(x<1\), \(|x-1|=1-x\), so the left derivative is \(-1\). The right derivative at \(1\) is \(2a+b\). Solve
\[
a+b=2,\qquad 2a+b=-1.
\]
Thus \(\boxed{a=-3,b=5}\).
